summary: Frontend-only retest (iteration 5) of the DJ Stew's Turntable 'burn the note on a too-early tap' anti-spam fix, run with Playwright on the public URL at 1920x1080. All requested checks pass. ANTI-SPAM PASSES: Space keydown every 90-290ms for a whole Master session (182 taps) scored 0/106 on time, 0 pts, 1 star, and all 5 dots turned red. Before the fix this was 93/93. Spamming pointerdown on the tap target on Pro (162 taps) scored 0/89, 0 pts, and every round failed. GENUINE PLAY STILL PASSES: Master scored 92/92 with 7176 pts, 3 stars and 88 sparkles, and the header streak chip climbed to 78x. Cadet scored 62/62 with 4926 pts and 3 stars. The patterns are random, so note counts differ from iteration_82, but accuracy is still 100%. SMOKE TESTS PASS: auto-repeat keydown claimed nothing (0 to 0). A round with no taps showed a red dot. Play Again reset the dots to yellow plus 4 grey. Change Level returned to the menu. No console errors appeared. NEW CRITICAL REGRESSION caused by this fix: a single extra or accidental tap ruins the rest of the round even when every other tap is perfectly timed. (a) Cadet: one tap on count-in beat 4 (at 2260ms, first note at 3750ms) followed by 11 perfectly timed taps scored 0 pts and failed the round. (b) Master: one accidental tap halfway between notes 2 and 3, with all 12 notes otherwise tapped perfectly, credited only 2 notes (50 pts) and failed the round. Kids who tap along with the count-in beeps, or double-tap once, will fail every round.

ui_bugs.issue: One extra tap shifts the tap-to-note matching by one for the rest of the round. Example: a stray tap burns note k. The player's on-time tap for note k then targets note k+1, which is one note-gap away and outside the tolerance window, so note k+1 is burned too. This repeats for every remaining note. Any early tap burns a note no matter how early it is, including taps during the count-in that come a full beat or more before the first note. Reproduced on Cadet: one tap during the count-in plus perfect taps gave 0 pts and a failed round. Reproduced on Master: one tap between notes plus perfect taps gave 2/12 notes and a failed round.

action_items: Change handleScratchTap so that one stray tap cannot shift the matching for every later note. Recommended fix: match each tap to the NEAREST non-rest note by |tapTime - expected| (claimed or not). If that note is unclaimed and diff <= tol, score it. Otherwise count the tap as a stray (strayCountRef++, streak reset, miss sound) WITHOUT burning any note. Then penalize accuracy in finishRound and sessionTally, e.g. correct = max(0, hits - strays) or total += strays. Spam would still fail, because many strays reach the 70% threshold. A single extra tap would cost only 1 point of accuracy instead of the whole round.

Alternative, smaller fix: only burn targetIdx when the tap lands in a narrow 'early zone' just before the window (e.g. expected - tol - BEAT_MS/2 <= tapTime < expected - tol). Taps earlier than that, including count-in taps, should be strays that don't burn a note but are still counted against accuracy.

Re-test after the fix: (1) Master spam 90-290ms must still fail, under 70%. (2) Genuine play must stay at 100%. (3) Genuine play plus 1 count-in tap must pass the round. (4) Genuine play plus 1 tap between notes must pass with 11/12 or similar.
critical_code_review_comments: The burn branch sets the target to the first unclaimed note with expected >= tapTime - tol. That target can be any distance in the future, so one tap 3 seconds early burns a note just like a tap 230ms early does.

Taps during the count-in phase are accepted (phase === 'countin') and also burn note 0. Combined with the issue above, tapping along with the count-in beeps, which is natural for children, fails the round.
The e.repeat guard, the round-dot colors and finishing the round early when all notes are claimed all still work correctly.

success_rate.frontend: All 4 requested checks pass. A new critical regression was found: one extra tap fails the round.

seed_data_creation: None. Only localStorage progress and stickers in the test browser.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Same setup as iteration_82: page.evaluate(dj_helpers.js) after load, click audio-unlock-overlay, wait 2.5s, then add_style_tag hiding tour-start-modal and player-name-prompt. Start a level with JS .click() on dj-turntable-difficulty-X. For a full session, use wait_for_selector('[data-testid=dj-turntable-complete]', timeout=200000); a Master session with genuine play takes about 110s. Results this iteration: Master spam 0/106; Pro pointer spam 0/89; Master genuine 92/92, 7176 pts; Cadet genuine 62/62, 4926 pts. Regression repro: in a one-shot interval, read __djRefs() once start and exp are set, then dispatch one Space at r.start+2250, or at the midpoint between note 2 and note 3, while __djAuto.mode='all'. Round 1 then turns red.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: Cadet with mode='all' plus one Space at count-in time 2260ms. Note 1 (3750ms) is burned. The perfect tap at 3750 then targets note 2 (4500ms), 750ms away, more than the 500ms tolerance, so note 2 is burned too, and so on for every note. Result: 0 pts, red dot. Root cause: tap matching is sequential (first unclaimed note), and a mistimed tap permanently consumes the next note no matter how far away it is, so one extra tap shifts the matching for every later note. Fix: match each tap to the nearest note, and make stray taps reduce accuracy without consuming notes (see action_items).
